subject: Re: Spike in self-serve credit redemptions — account cluster (NimbleBox)
messages:
From: Evan Marsh <evan.marsh@nimblebox.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:15:00Z
Subject: Unusual mass redemptions of trial credits tied to NimbleBox emails

Hi Vivek —

We're seeing a cluster of freshly created accounts on Redwood redeeming the self-serve trial credits using email addresses that reference nimblebox (e.g. user+test01@nimblebox.io, user+ci@nimblebox.io) and a handful of disposable domains. Our QA team is running automation today but the volume triggered something on our side and we wanted to flag it and understand whether these redemptions are allowed under your promo terms.

We have ~120 redemptions in the last 3 hours from a handful of IP ranges. Example addresses attached. Can you confirm:
- Are these unique trial grants per email, or did your system allow repeat grants from similar device fingerprints?
- If this looks like abuse, can we reverse credits for the affected accounts or get a list so our ops team can correlate?

Attaching a short sample of the signups we captured.

Thanks,
Evan Marsh
QA Lead, NimbleBox

Date: 2026-11-05T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Unusual mass redemptions of trial credits tied to NimbleBox emails

Evan —

Thanks for the heads up and for the sample. I'm looping in our fraud and infra teams to triage immediately. Initial asks: can you confirm whether those addresses were created by your CI/QA automation (names of job runs) and if there are any related session IDs? That will help us map our logs.

Marissa / Aditya / Priyom / Mina — FYI: NimbleBox reporting ~120 redemptions in a short window. They attached a CSV sample; marked as potentially legitimate (QA), but it looks like duplicate pattern + disposable domains. Please run the quick triage (IP patterns, device fingerprint reuse, and whether credits were auto-issued by the self-serve path). If we confirm abuse, recommend temporarily suspend issuance for the affected IP blocks and flag accounts for review.

Can we have a short summary and the raw signup events by 12:00 PST? Evan — we'll share anything we can but may need you to map to your job names.

— Vivek
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Evan Marsh <evan.marsh@nimblebox.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Unusual mass redemptions of trial credits tied to NimbleBox emails

Thanks — quick triage notes from my side before Aditya drops logs:

- Pattern: many emails use plus-addressing (user+ci@nimblebox.io) and a cluster of ~18 disposable domains. That pattern often maps to automated QA but is also used for lightweight fraud.
- Action recommended: pause any further self-serve credit issuance from the implicated IP ranges and enable rate-limits for new signups from those ranges.
- Evidence we need to decide on reversals: (1) full signup timestamps + IPs, (2) first-token-generation times, (3) whether the same device fingerprint or billing metadata repeated.

If NimbleBox confirms these are internal CI tests, we can offer a one-time bulk credit grant for their test environment and mark those accounts as exempt; if not, we should revoke credits and close the accounts.

Evan — can you confirm which CI runs created these? If you can provide job names or a narrow time window, it'll speed the mapping.

Marissa Cole
Lead, Fraud & Risk | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Evan Marsh <evan.marsh@nimblebox.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T13:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Unusual mass redemptions of trial credits tied to NimbleBox emails

On Thu, 2026-11-05 at 11:08, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Thanks — quick triage notes from my side before Aditya drops logs:

I've pulled the backend events and attached a compact CSV of signup events and token-issuance timestamps. Summary: 126 signups between 2026-11-05T07:40:12Z and 2026-11-05T10:05:03Z. 92% of the signups came from three CIDR blocks that resolve to a CI provider we whitelist for some customers; fingerprints are largely identical (same UA string + repeating ephemeral device id).

Preliminary conclusion: looks like a legitimate CI-driven burst, not credential stuffing from external bad actors. However — our system currently treats plus-addressing as unique emails for self-serve credit grants and does not de-duplicate by base address. That made the automation appear as many unique users.

Attached: signup_events_20261105.csv (sample, first 200 rows) and session_logs_20261105.txt.

Recommendation:
- If this is NimbleBox CI, we'll mark the cluster as internal and reverse the flagged enforcement.
- Short-term config change: dedupe self-serve credit grants by base email (strip +tags) for domains in a customer allowlist; rate-limit per device fingerprint for newly created accounts.

- Aditya
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime

From: Evan Marsh <evan.marsh@nimblebox.io>

Date: 2026-11-05T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Unusual mass redemptions of trial credits tied to NimbleBox emails

Thanks — confirmed this was our nightly regression CI (job: regression/nightly/burst-tests) that spun up ephemeral accounts to exercise throttling. Sorry for the alarm; we should have prefixed those addresses with .test to avoid plus-tag confusion.

We'd appreciate the one-time bulk grant for our test environment rather than asking our ops team to recreate thousands of test accounts. If you can provide a scoped grant (NBX-internal-test, expiration 90 days) and a list of the affected accounts to mark as exempt, that'll solve the issue.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to sign an MoU for test environment rules if that helps.

— Evan
Evan Marsh
QA Lead, NimbleBox
